items.label: Data release
items.headline: New: the DMV Employer Cost Index 2026
items.cardSub: What one employee costs an employer in statutory taxes, paid leave and wage floors in DC, Maryland and Virginia. Every figure sourced.
items.text:
New: the DMV Employer Cost Index 2026

What does one employee cost an employer in statutory taxes in DC, Maryland and Virginia? We built the answer from primary sources.

- New-employer unemployment insurance: DC 2.90% on $9,000, MD 2.60% on $8,500, VA 2.73% on $8,000
- DC Paid Family Leave: 0.75% of wages, employer-paid
- Maryland FAMLI: 0.90% from 2027

Every figure links to its source. Free, no sign-up.

Source: DC DOES; Maryland Department of Labor; Virginia Employment Commission

Read the index: https://peonomics.com/dmv-employer-cost-index

items.label: Countdown
items.headline: 1 month until binders are due for Jan. 1 renewals
items.text:
1 month until binders are due for Jan. 1 renewals

If your health plan renews Jan. 1, finalize it this week. Carriers typically want final plan selections and the binder payment in early December, and your people need time to see their options and pick a plan before then.

This week:
- Lock the plan lineup and what the company contributes
- Put each option and its cost per paycheck in front of your people
- Set their election deadline a few days ahead of the binder date

For scale: the average 2026 employer-sponsored premium is $9,804 for single coverage and $28,303 for family. Employers pay $8,132 and $20,832 of that on average.

Source: KFF Employer Health Benefits Survey 2026

Renewal quotes in hand? Compare them side by side: https://peonomics.com/compare

items.label: Key date
items.headline: Tuesday, Nov. 10: the Labor Department sets 2026 FUTA credit reductions
items.text:
Tuesday, Nov. 10: the Labor Department sets 2026 FUTA credit reductions

Nov. 10 is the date the Department of Labor checks which states still owe federal unemployment loans. Employers in those states lose part of their FUTA credit and pay more for 2026.

Base FUTA: 0.6% on the first $7,000 per employee.
California's statutory step for 2026: an extra 1.5%, an estimate until DOL confirms.

Source: U.S. Department of Labor; Federal Register 2026-00342

Every state's rates, sourced: https://peonomics.com/data-library

items.headline: What one employee costs an employer in Washington, DC, before the extras
items.cardTitle: Washington, DC: the base cost of one employee
items.cardSub: Average private-sector pay, employer FICA and the employer share of single health coverage at firms under 50 employees.
items.text:
What one employee costs an employer in Washington, DC, before the extras

In Washington, DC, three numbers every employer cost starts from:

- Average private-sector pay per job: $123,844 a year (includes part-time jobs)
- Employer Social Security and Medicare on that pay (7.65%): $9,474
- Employer share of single health coverage at firms under 50 employees: $7,475 a year

That is $140,793 before unemployment insurance, workers' comp, retirement, admin or a PEO fee. The Washington, DC page carries the rest, each figure with its source.

Source: BLS QCEW 2025 annual averages, private; AHRQ MEPS-IC 2025, state tables; 26 U.S.C. 3111

items.label: Countdown
items.headline: 1 month until the Social Security wage base rises to $192,300
items.text:
1 month until the Social Security wage base rises to $192,300

On Jan. 1, 2027 the cap on wages subject to the 6.2% employer Social Security tax moves from $184,500 to $192,300.

For each employee paid above the cap, the employer's maximum Social Security tax goes from $11,439.00 to $11,922.60: $483.60 more per head.

Source: Social Security Administration

See what it does to your payroll: https://peonomics.com/#cost-lab

items.label: Countdown
items.headline: 30 days until Virginia's minimum wage rises to $13.75
items.text:
30 days until Virginia's minimum wage rises to $13.75

Virginia's minimum wage moves from $12.77 to $13.75 an hour on Jan. 1, 2027, then to $15.00 on Jan. 1, 2028.

For a full-time worker at the floor (2,080 hours a year), that is $2,038 more in annual wages, before payroll taxes rise with it.

Source: Office of the Governor of Virginia, HB1/SB1

Wage floors for every DMV jurisdiction: https://peonomics.com/dmv-employer-cost-index

items.label: Key date
items.headline: Starting Jan. 1, Maryland employers pay into FAMLI
items.text:
Starting Jan. 1, Maryland employers pay into FAMLI

Starting Jan. 1, 2027, Maryland employers remit FAMLI contributions: 0.90% of wages up to the Social Security wage base ($192,300 in 2027).

Employers with 15 or more employees pay at least half (0.45%) and may withhold the rest from pay. That is up to $865.35 per employee at the wage cap. Smaller employers owe no employer share but must remit what they withhold. Benefits begin by Jan. 3, 2028.

Source: Maryland FAMLI law via Jackson Lewis; SSA 2027 wage base

DC, MD and VA employer costs, side by side: https://peonomics.com/dmv-employer-cost-index

Average pay per retail job in Maryland: $44,351 a year, against $78,676 across all private industries (includes part-time jobs).

Employer Social Security and Medicare on that pay: $3,393. Payroll taxes, unemployment insurance and workers' comp are all priced as a share of pay, so this is the first number to check in any PEO quote.

Source: BLS QCEW 2025 annual averages, private; 26 U.S.C. 3111

What one employee costs an employer in North Carolina, before the extras

items.headline: 60 days until Virginia's minimum wage reaches $15.00
items.text:
60 days until Virginia's minimum wage reaches $15.00

Virginia's minimum wage steps from $13.75 to $15.00 an hour on Jan. 1, 2028.

At 2,080 hours a year, that is $2,600 more per full-time employee at the floor, before payroll taxes.

Source: Office of the Governor of Virginia, HB1/SB1

items.text:
60 days until Maryland FAMLI benefits begin

Maryland FAMLI benefits begin by Jan. 3, 2028. Contributions began Jan. 1, 2027: 0.90% of wages, with employers of 15 or more paying at least 0.45%.

Leave policies, payroll setup and coverage for absent staff need to be settled before claims start.

Source: Maryland FAMLI law via Jackson Lewis
